title: This Underrated Region of Portugal Has Roman Ruins, Hilltop Villages, and Some of the Country's Best Beaches
text:
Plan an Alentejo, Portugal trip with stops in Évora, Monsaraz, Melides, wineries, beaches, and boutique hotels.
Some of my earliest memories are of warm summer evenings in Campo Maior, a historic town deep in the Alentejo region of Portugal. As my grandmother cooked her many variations ofa regional bread stew, I would sit on the porch looking at storks nesting on the chimneys across the street, while my grandfather complained about the prices of olives and grapes.
“Maybe better next year,” he used to say. I didn’t know what slow travel was back then, but after more than 15 years of planning trips, I believe that Alentejo is one of Portugal’s best-kept gems. Here is my guide for an incredible getaway to the Alentejo region.is the capital of the Alentejo region and a good starting point for any trip.
It’s less than 100 miles from Lisbon, and the surrounding countryside is a landscape of gentle rolling hills, seemingly endless cork oaks and olive groves, and villages of whitewashed buildings. Évora is best explored on foot, allowing you to browse local shops, visit artisans, and encounter well-preserved Roman ruins, including the Roman Temple of Évora, near the center of town. The best lunch spot in Évora may be a matter of perennial debate, but the underratedgets my vote.
It’s known for traditional cuisine, especially its roasted suckling pig. Head about 40 miles east, and you’ll find yourself amid seemingly endless vineyards and some of the region’s most impressive places to stay. I recommend, where you can book a room, suite, or cottage and enjoy the on-site pool, spa, and the estate’s deep connection to the surrounding landscape. Stunning views of Monsaraz, a medieval village, in Alentejo, Portugal.
Credit: Photogilio/iStockphoto/Getty Images Your second day can be spent in Monsaraz, a hilltop medieval village that overlooks Lake Alqueva, Europe’s largest artificial lake. If you’re interested in history, there are plenty of museums and megalithic sites to visit in and around Monsaraz, including one of the area’s tallest standing stones, along with a 14th-century castle.
After exploring Monsaraz, head downhill to the small village of Corval, where you can take a pottery class before having a picnic dinner and stargazing with a local astronomer. , a winery, restaurant, and art center. The wines here—I prefer the reds—are as bold as the contemporary-art collection. Make a reservation for a wine-paired lunch overlooking the vineyards as you bid farewell to the Alentejo.
After lunch, head west toward the Atlantic coast and the Santo André Lagoon. White-sand beaches and blue waters offer a striking contrast to the inland landscapes you’ve just left behind—but rest assured, you’re still in the Alentejo. In the small town of Melides, book a stay atBirds resting at the Lagoon of Santo Andre. Credit: Néstor MN/Adobe Stock In Melides, you’ll experience a different side of the Alentejo.
Here, the only things that seem to matter are the rhythm of the sea and absolute tranquility. Relax by the sea and indulge in a hearty meal at local favoritewhich serves traditional Portuguese cuisine such as oven-roasted duck. Or you can explore the town of Comporta, another coastal destination, where you can trysea bass grilled over hot coals.
My favorite place for a sunset dinner is farther south, in the town of Vila Nova de Milfontes, where whitewashed houses line the streets. For the return trip to Lisbon, driving is easiest, though taking the ferry from the Tróia Peninsula, just north of Melides, makes for a more scenic route—you might even spot a dolphin gliding alongside the ferry. After disembarking in Setúbal, stroll through the city’s Mercado do Livramento. Stop foroysters for a light lunch before flying out.
Lisbon’s Humberto Delgado Airport is about 50 minutes away by car.is a member of Travel + Leisure’s A-List and specializes in trips to Portugal. You can create a tailor-made itinerary with Nuno by contacting hello@thedtailor.pt.
